claim_reviews.rationale: Passenger statement and Fulton 1810 identify an operating boat and its maker; the description attributes the 1804 engine identification to Fulton rather than asserting the original machine ledger was examined.

New York State Library transcript of its American Citizen September 2 issue advertises Friday September 4, Paulas Hook and seven dollars to Albany. Offer is not actual payment; later guide repeats same offer.

Printed 1855 reprint of 5 September passenger statement recounts Friday New York departure and Albany arrival, and identifies it as first passage as a packet. Date is source-supported; no claim of actual fare or overall first steamboat. Newspaper original not examined.

Fulton in his September 1810 letter identifies a 24-inch by four-foot 1804 Boulton & Watt engine with his passenger boat. The 1805 account and forwarding letter provide maker side and say goods forwarded toward London, not proof of arrival, freight, or fitting. The event date is the letter date.

A supplier contribution belongs to the stage where supply occurred, not the later documented-description event, which records Fulton writing a letter in 1810. Remove contribution while retaining attributed maker identification; alternatively add a separately sourced 1805 dispatch event limited to forwarding toward London and attach the contribution to that event. Do not state delivery or installation was verified.

The code, transatlantic freight and installation remain unverified. Maker-side order/forwarding and buyer-side later identification establish stronger supply evidence than shared dimensions alone; exact identity with a different Soho installation is not shown.

Reusable entry fields and stops require specific matching and independent duty evidence; reject common numbers and advertisements alone. Science Museum object 1862-53/1 is a traceable different Comet engine pilot, not proof of its operation schedule.
Instructions generalize port-record checks; 1808 enrollment transcription identifies remodeled vessel and prior enrollment 973 from 1807, while the passenger text uses Clermont as a landing.

Maker catalogue describes alphabetical and repeated code systems, order books and alternative small-engine sequence; calendar MS 3147/3/496 lists Fulton/Francis correspondence and drawings. No particular code assigned. Item MS 3147/4/91 page could not be loaded by reviewer; its exact item date and access status remain an access limitation, not independently verified.
Maker account and letters document order and dispatch via carrier for London in 1805, not transatlantic receipt or fitting; distinction of these steps is sound.

Fulton’s 1810 buyer statement explicitly ties 1804 engine to Hudson passenger service and requests another; matching dimensions alone are not an identity test. U.S. National Museum bulletin identifies drawing 180137 as remodeled North River, not original installation. Multiple copies of 1810 letter are one underlying source.

Contemporary advertisement is an offer; independent passenger testimony is preserved in a later reprint and records first packet passage. Source roles and later reproduction are stated, and no exact maker code, installed-object identity or ticket purchase is claimed.

The source metadata identifies the advertisement facsimile/transcript, Dickinson printed transcriptions, and Munsell 1855 reprint separately; PDF and JPEG checksums match local originals. The 1807 original passenger newspaper issue and actual manuscripts remain uninspected.
